title: Geo-compliant routing engine: EU-only residency + allowlist/denylist enforcement
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Several enterprise customers and EU-regulated customers require strict geo-compliance: requests originating from or labeled as EU-only must be routed to EU-resident execution zones, and associated data must not leave EU regions. In addition, some customers operate allowlists/denylists for control plane tenants (e.g., allowed model variants or allowed regions) that must be enforced at routing time.

Goal: Implement a deterministic, low-latency routing constraint layer in the smart router that enforces geo-residency policies and customer-level allowlist/denylist rules while preserving SLOs and compatibility with tier-based routing and fallback model variants. This ticket covers the core runtime policy evaluation, audit logging, and a minimal admin API for allowlist management.

Scope: This work includes: (1) policy expression for EU-only residency and data residency tags on requests; (2) evaluation precedence between global tier rules, customer allowlists/denylists, and automated fallback variants; (3) per-request audit entries for compliance attestations; (4) integration tests and e2e on a staging EU region; (5) a lightweight admin endpoint for CS/SE to set per-customer allowlists/denylists. Not in scope: full Console UI, RBAC for admin endpoint (handled in follow-up), and long-term storage of audit logs beyond retention window (handled by logging infra).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Requests tagged or matched as EU-only are routed exclusively to EU-hosted capacity (hosted + dedicated EU pools).
- Customer-level allowlist/denylist entries override default model routing and block disallowed variants at evaluation time.
- If an allowed model is unavailable in the required region, routing fails open only with explicit customer opt-in (controlled by a per-customer fallback flag). Otherwise, requests receive a 409 with a clear error code and remediation suggestion.
- Each routed request generates a compliance audit record with request_id, customer_id, matched_policy, chosen_region, chosen_model_variant, and timestamp. Audit records are emitted to the observability pipeline with structured fields.
- Unit and integration tests cover precedence scenarios (global tier vs customer allowlist vs denylist) and latency regression <5ms on policy evaluation path.

Design notes:
- Introduce a lightweight policy descriptor (flat list of labels and flags) attached to customer profiles in the routing cache. Keep descriptors small to avoid expensive lookups during high-throughput serving.
- Evaluation precedence: denylist > allowlist > customer fallback flag > global routing policies. This ensures explicit prohibitions win.
- Use region tagging on execution pools; extend existing pool selector to accept a region constraint and model-variant constraints.
- Audit entries are emitted asynchronously to the existing event pipeline (kafka topic: routing-compliance). Include a sampling key for high-volume customers to avoid X% of traffic overload; however, all blocked/failure events are always logged.

Implementation plan:
1) Schema: add customer_policy descriptor to customer config service and populate cache (ENG-9012 integration).
2) Router changes: policy-evaluation middleware that short-circuits incompatible pools before cost/latency scoring.
3) Admin API: POST /admin/customers/:id/policy (internal-only) for allowlist/denylist/fallback toggle.
4) Tests: unit policy engine tests; staging e2e with dedicated EU pool; perf microbenchmark.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: policy evaluation adds latency to hot path. Mitigation: cache evaluated decision per-request-hash for 30s and micro-optimize the evaluation path in C++ hot code (or Rust shim).
- Risk: inconsistent policy state across nodes. Mitigation: use consistent invalidation via pubsub + versioned policy descriptors.
- Risk: accidental open fallback leaking EU data. Mitigation: require explicit per-customer opt-in flag and confirm via sign-off from Compliance.

Monitoring & rollout:
- Metrics: routing_policy_eval_latency_ms (p95), routing_policy_blocked_count by reason, routing_compliance_audit_events_count.
- Rollout: Canary in staging EU -> canary on 5% traffic for a subset of customers -> 25% -> full, gated by no increase in blocked false-positives and latency regressions.

Notes: See design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Geo+Residency+Routing+Draft and initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/842
